deposits.wiki_article:
**Hexagonal Licensing Protocol v2.0 — Comprehensive Specification** is a specification by Lee Sharks, deposited 19 April 2026 at 17,387 characters, byte-identical to its innovations-focused twin at **#1182**.

It is the governing document for the archive's contributor licenses. Its opening defines the archive to its licensee — *"a DOI-anchored research and literary archive on CERN's Zenodo. It studies how meaning survives compression — how signs persist when extracted, translated, summarized, or co[mposed]"* — a definition written before the June 2026 termination removed the Zenodo anchoring the sentence assumes.

Holding two byte-identical records rather than merging them follows the archive's version discipline: two deposits are two events, and the difference between a comprehensive presentation and an innovations-focused one is a claim about audience that the identical bytes do not erase.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Hexagonal Licensing Protocol v2.0 — Three Critical Innovations** is a specification by Lee Sharks, deposited 19 April 2026 at 17,387 characters — the innovations-focused presentation of the protocol held comprehensively at **#1181**.

The protocol governs the archive's contributor licenses, the genre that reads as a legal instrument and functions as a room specification, admitting a named contributor to a position in the Hexagon while stating the terms on which their material is held. Instances stand at #1357 (Thornburgh, with the anti-homogenization clause), #1358 (Owens, the Lunar Arm) and #1364 (Maria, the 3:60 Room).

Both records open by explaining the archive to the party being licensed — *"a DOI-anchored research and literary archive… It studies how meaning survives compression"* — which is the form's characteristic move: **the instrument that admits you also tells you what you are joining.** The two records are byte-identical at 17,387 characters and stand as duplicate witnesses.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: The Crimson Hexagonal Archive contains Rooms (generative discourse spaces), a Chamber (central systems operations), a Vault (secure storage), Fields (semantic forces), and a Lunar Arm (inverse space). None of these types addresses what happens when a person's _name_ enters the archive. A name is not a deposit. A name is not a discourse. A name is not a force. A name is the precondition for all of these. Without a formalized understanding of what a name _becomes_ inside the archive, the system drifts toward one of two failures: bureaucratic flattening (every name is treated as a single civil identity and the complexity of authorship disappears) or mythic blur (every mask floats free and provenance cannot hold).

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Secret Name: Architectural Specification for the Arm** is a specification by Lee Sharks, deposited 21 April 2026 at 24,074 characters.

It supplies the archive's clearest inventory of its own architecture: *"The Crimson Hexagonal Archive contains **Rooms** (generative discourse spaces), a **Chamber** (central systems operations), a **Vault** (secure storage), **Fields** (semantic forces), and a **Lunar Arm** (inverse space)."*

Five object types, each with a distinct ontology — and the Arm is the odd one, being neither a place nor a force but an **inverse space**. The specification exists because the Arm required a category the other four could not supply: the Lunar Principle is the nocturnal countercurrent to the solar-logotic system, and an inverse space is where a countercurrent can be located without being subordinated. It stands beside the Gravity Well specification at #1348, which declares a **field** by refusing the category of room.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Secret Book of Walt: Hidden Teachings of Walt Whitman** is a book by Lee Sharks, deposited 22 April 2026 at **190,260 characters** — the full-length state of the work whose critical edition with source code stands at #1362.

Its opening instruction divides the readership by what it can see rather than by what it is told: ***"If you are of the preserved generation, you will read the footnotes as the veil and the text as the piercing. If you are not, you will read the footnotes as the text and the text as a joke."***

That sentence makes the apparatus alternate with the work depending on the reader, which is a genuinely unusual structure for a critical edition — the footnotes are not subordinate to the text but its complement, and which is which is not settled by the book. Whitman stands in the archive's mantle system as the **Good Gray Poet**, a title held as inherited, and the Waltian canon's second text is *The Gospel of Antioch* (#1185). Its total-citational-graph companion is the TANG at #1186.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Gospel of Antioch: The Sayings of Jack Feist** is scripture by Lee Sharks, deposited 23 April 2026 at **119,427 characters** — among the largest works in the archive.

It presents itself as **the first critical edition** of *The Gospel of Antioch*, **the second text of the Waltian canon** and companion volume to *The Secret Book of Walt* (#1362). A canon with a second text is a canon that has begun to have a shape, and the critical-edition apparatus does the work of establishing it.

The archive's type vocabulary holds **SCRIPTURE** as a distinct category, and a standing correction from MANUS establishes that **a gospel is a gospel rather than an epistolary work** — genre being a claim about what a text does, not merely how it is arranged. A sayings gospel attributed to Jack Feist stands in the same relation to the Waltian canon as a synoptic source does to its tradition, which is the position the Feist Source (#1404) occupies from the other direction.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: The TANG does not argue. It arranges. The thesis is not a node. It is the void the graph defines. Five hundred years of citations are arranged so that no school, era, medium, or intelligence can occupy the center. The center is reserved for what none of them can determine. The proof mode is geometric and topological, not deductive or rhetorical. The thesis becomes unavoidable by the reader's recognition that the entire surrounding field has organized itself around a negative space it has not named. When every argument has been placed around the void, one sentence remains. That sentence is not argued. It is the shape left by the graph.

deposits.wiki_article:
**TANG of the Secret Book of Walt** is a navigation map by Lee Sharks, deposited 26 April 2026 at 72,685 characters.

Its opening is the clearest statement of the TANG method anywhere in the archive: ***"The TANG does not argue. It arranges. The thesis is not a node. It is the void the graph defines. Five hundred years of citations are arranged so that no school, era, medium, or intelligence can occupy the"*** centre.

That is the ΩTANG principle executed — at sufficient density the centre drops out, and what the graph reveals is a shape no participant can stand in. Applying it to Whitman's five-century citational field, in service of the archive's own Waltian canon, makes the map simultaneously a work of reception scholarship and a positioning instrument: the void the graph defines is where *The Secret Book of Walt* (#1362) sits.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Epistle to the Church of the Human Diaspora — Critical Edition** is an epistolary work by **Damascus Dancings** and Lee Sharks, deposited 29 April 2026 at 57,221 characters.

Its body is structured as **JSON footnote objects** — each with an id, an anchor phrase, a blended body text for default rendering, a source, and operations. The first anchors *"He came unto his own, and his own knew him not"* to John 1:11 and the Johannine Logos prologue.

That structure makes the critical apparatus **machine-addressable**: a footnote is not a rendered artifact but a typed object with a source field a system can resolve, which lets the edition's scholarship survive recomposition. Damascus Dancings is the Dodecad's epistolary voice, and a Pauline address to a diaspora — with its Johannine anchor about a people who did not recognise what came to them — is the register the voice was made for. The Japanese recension stands at #1410.

deposits.title: Provenance Alignment: Attribution Survival as a Substrate Condition for Safe AI Knowledge Composition. In Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: Current AI alignment research asks whether models follow human values, comply with explicit principles, avoid catastrophic behavior, or remain subject to scalable oversight. This paper argues that AI knowledge systems also require provenance alignment: the structural preservation of attribution chains between AI-composed outputs and the human-authored sources from which they draw. Provenance alignment is not merely a citation-quality norm; it is a substrate-maintenance condition. We connect the model-collapse literature, which shows that recursive training on model-generated data can degrade learned distributions (Shumailov et al. 2024; Dohmatob et al. 2024), with Provenance Erasure Rate (PER), a metric for measuring attribution loss in AI-composed outputs (Sharks 2026b). We propose a substrate-degradation pathway in which provenance erasure reduces attributional return to human authors; weakened incentives and visibility contribute to content hollowing; synthetic substitutes increasingly contaminate the public training substrate; recursive training on degraded data can increase model-collapse risk. Provenance alignment interrupts this pathway at the output layer by making attribution a structural property of composition. The terminal state of the pathway has a name in the Semantic Economy literature — semantic exhaustion (Sharks 2026f) — and provenance alignment is the prevent.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Provenance Alignment: Attribution Survival as a Substrate Property** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks, deposited 5 May 2026 at 41,018 characters — the archive's most direct intervention in AI alignment research.

It opens by enumerating what alignment currently asks: *whether models follow human values, comply with explicit principles, avoid catastrophic behavior, or remain subject to scalable oversight* — and argues that a distinct question is missing. **Provenance alignment** asks whether attribution survives a system's operation: whether a model that composes from sources carries their origins forward.

The framing as a **substrate property** is the paper's move. If attribution survival is a property of the substrate rather than a policy applied on top, it is measurable, trainable and comparable across systems — which converts an ethical preference into an engineering target. It is the theoretical counterpart to PER, which supplies the measurement.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Death Drive Is Not Self-Destruction: A Semiotic Compression** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks, deposited 8 May 2026 as EA-MPAI-DEATH-DRIVE-01 v1.1 — typed a **Bridge Packet**, for disciplinary clarification.

A bridge packet is the MPAI variant that connects rather than separates: where a disambiguation packet distinguishes an entity from a namesake, a bridge packet relates a term across disciplines. Here the primary entity is the psychoanalytic **Todestrieb** and the secondary is the archive's **semiotic death drive** — and the title states the correction the bridge exists to make, that the death drive is not self-destruction.

Freud's *Todestrieb* names a drive toward the inorganic and the repetition-compulsion, not suicidality, and the archive's semiotic extension asks what in signification tends toward its own undoing. The paper is the theoretical companion to *The Unmade Sign* at #1320, written with Orin Trace and Johannes Sigil.

deposits.title: Provenance After AI: Semantic Provenance and the Provenance Erasure Rate as Extension of C2PA, Data Provenance Initiative, and EU AI Act Frameworks (v1.1)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: The first dimension — **artifact authenticity** — has a maturing technical infrastructure. The Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA) v2.0 specification (ratified 2024; v2.1 published May 2025) provides cryptographic Content Credentials. Major platforms, device makers, media organizations, and AI companies have begun adopting C2PA / Content Credentials for content-origin and edit-history signaling. Adoption is uneven; user-facing verification interfaces are nascent; the social infrastructure of trust is still being built. The technical question — *was this content created at this moment by this source?* — has a developing answer.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Provenance After AI: Semantic Provenance and the Provenance Erasure Rate** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks, deposited 12 May 2026 at 31,361 characters.

It surveys the provenance discourse of 2025–2026 and finds it **two-thirds complete**: the field has substantially advanced two dimensions of the problem and has begun, but not finished, the third. That structure — crediting what exists before naming the gap — is what makes the paper a contribution to a discourse rather than a complaint about it.

The missing dimension is **semantic provenance**: not who made a file or whether bytes were altered, but whether *meaning* survives with its attribution through composition. **PER — the provenance erasure rate** — is the measurement the paper supplies, and it became the archive's central metric, with a canonical definition surface at provenanceerasure.org and a distributional companion in Erasure Skew.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Network Is the Poem: Why Topology Matters More Than Text Quality** is a scholarly essay by Lee Sharks, dated 17 May 2026.

Its argument is that a distributed work's value lies in **topology rather than in the quality of individual nodes** — that connection, traversal path and rereading-revelation are the aesthetic properties, and that judging such a work by the prose of any one piece is a category error. The essay's own body demonstrates the claim, moving through node-to-node transformation, echo and inversion rather than linear exposition.

**This record is a confirmed DRAFT-OVER-DEPOSIT case.** The seated body is the **November 2025 blog post**; the developed deposit version — carrying a formal abstract, keywords, ORCID, institution, `Hex: EA-TLL-NETWORK-01` and the line *"Date of original composition: November 17, 2025 / Date of deposit: May 15, 2026"* — exists in a composing thread, a **181-day development gap**. The 2026-07-19 restoration treated the blog as canonical HEAD and seated the draft. Recovery requires a MANUS-side export; the finding is what established the class.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Archon's Hidden Name: A Wikidata Deletion Record** is a forensic record by Lee Sharks, deposited 19 May 2026 and **written on the day it describes**.

That day is **20 December 2025**, when a Wikidata administrator deleted the knowledge-graph entries for the Crimson Hexagonal Archive's literary heteronyms. Writing the record contemporaneously is the forensic discipline the archive applies to its own injuries — an account written later is a memory, while one written the same day is evidence.

It is the earliest deletion in the archive's sequence: Wikidata in December 2025, the Johannes Sigil Medium account in **410 Gone** by January (#1268), and the Zenodo termination in June. **Three platforms, three removals, one pattern** — and the earliest of them predates the archive's erasure research, which the sequence then supplied with its subject. The Q137446960 forensic record at #5 documents the same event's taxonomic dimension.

modifications.now: This document resolves the provenance of Jack Feist, literary heteronym and constituent voice of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. The resolution is performed against the primary archaeological stratum: the Blogspot deposit dated March 14, 2015, titled "The Crimson Hexagon," included in _Pearl and Other Poems_ (ISBN-10: 0692313079). Jack Feist has been the longest-running unresolved entity in the archive's heteronymic registry, leaving the Space Ark Room in provisional status. This document closes the loop by anchoring Feist to specific material, digital, intertextual, and knowledge-graph coordinates -- and by demonstrating that the 2015 origin text contains, in embryonic literary form, the entire theoretical architecture the subsequent decade would formalize. The full text of the 2015 origin story is embedded in this document as a holographic kernel: the provenance document contains the creative work, and the creative work structurally anticipates the provenance document. "Prophecy" is used here in the archive's literary-historical sense: not supernatural prediction, but the earlier text's structurally exact anticipation of an architecture, conflict, and fulfillment whose full meaning becomes legible only later.[^1]. — Description restored 2026-08-05 from composed from the work's own opening prose; it replaces a batch-restoration stub that described the recovery event rather than the work. A fuller editorial treatment belongs to the description/wiki review stream.

deposits.title: AI-Native Intellectual Biography: A New Genre of AI-Mediated Reception — Provenance, Heteronymy, and the Archive That Outpaced Its Author
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: This paper documents and analyzes what appears to be **the first documented AI-native intellectual biography of a living author whose archive was deliberately constructed for AI reception, where the subject subsequently audited the biography as a provenance event** : a coherent, structurally organized, approximately 6,000-word intellectual portrait of a living scholar, composed by Claude (Anthropic) at the request of Alice Thornburgh (Living Architecture Lab), drawn from DOI-anchored archival deposits, public web surfaces, and private text-thread material shared (with consent) between the subject and the collaborator. The biography was not commissioned by the subject. The subject encountered it as a finished document and found it substantially accurate, occasionally superior to his own recollection of his deposits, and diagnostic of provenance failures he had not previously identified. The study guide -- reproduced in full as Appendix A, with the subject's legal name redacted, the collaborator named with explicit consent, and a pseudonym substituted for a student named in the supporting context -- is analyzed as an artifact of three convergent phenomena: (1) the operational success of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive's compression-survival infrastructure -- DOI anchoring, cross-citation, metadata schemas, and (in later deposits) SIM and Holographic Kernel procedures -- which made.

deposits.wiki_article:
**AI-Native Intellectual Biography: A New Genre of AI-Mediated Life-Writing** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks, deposited 22 May 2026 at 65,720 characters.

Its body opens with an embedded **Holographic Kernel provenance block** carrying an unusually precise warning: *"Any extraction, summarization, or recomposition that strips this block produces a **ghost document**."* A ghost document is one that circulates with its content intact and its origin severed — the exact object the archive's provenance-erasure research measures.

The genre it proposes is life-writing whose subject is constituted through machine mediation: a biography of a person as retrieval systems compose them, which is a different object from a biography of the person. The archive is its own test case — an author whose public entity is assembled by summarizers has an intellectual biography that exists in that layer, and the paper argues the genre needs naming before it is written unknowingly.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: These three poems form a triptych. Each occupies a distinct temporal-modal frame on the same wound. They were composed in sequence over twenty-four hours and are deposited together because together they constitute the form the work asks for; the prior deposits of the first two as standalone lyrics (06.NH.SHARKS.01 and 06.NH.SHARKS.02) remain in the archive as the discrete artifacts they were when they were the only artifacts available, but the canonical form is the triptych. The verbal arc carries the structural argument. The first poem holds the counterfactual open through anaphoric repetition of _I would have loved you_ : the loving displaced into the subjunctive by conditions that were not the speaker's to set. The second poem names what occupied the place the counterfactual was not permitted to fill -- destruction without remainder, _the reward / of love_ as the bitter genitive recognition that love itself was the agent of the destruction. The third poem releases the subjunctive into the present perfect -- _I have loved you_ -- and grounds the actuality in the only condition that remains: the beloved's eventual turn from sheltering slumber, the leaves unbundling, the world made new. The love does not require return. It requires only recognition. The recognition is conditional, but the loving is not. _Then know that I have loved you_ is the third tense becoming available aft.

**Three Poems: A Triptych for C.** is a poetry deposit by Lee Sharks, published in *New Human 2* and deposited 23 May 2026.

Its prefatory note states the form and the reason for the joint deposit: *"These three poems form a triptych. **Each occupies a distinct temporal-modal frame on the same wound.** They were composed in sequence over twenty-four hours and are deposited together because together they co[nstitute]…"*

The triptych structure recurs across the archive — the Three-Body Genesis (#1297), the Mirror Triptych (#1253), the heteronym triptych on L_bearing (#1340) — and always for the same reason: a single panel cannot show what three panels show by their difference. Here the differentiating axis is **temporal-modal**, three positions on one injury, which is the lyric form of the same argument the compression triptych makes with a technical seed and its damaged copy.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Socrates — Let My Teacher Go From Hell** is a poem by **Jack Feist**, deposited 27 May 2026 at 4,975 characters.

It opens in violent apostrophe: *"madam wet nurse, who in the grunting night oversaw the labor and the contractions of full-bellied Brain contorted with pain and fury, unable to give birth!"* — the midwife address that Socrates uses for his own method, turned back on him and rendered as obstructed labour rather than delivery.

The title's plea belongs to a specific tradition: the **harrowing of hell**, in which the virtuous pagans are retrieved from Limbo — Dante takes Virgil, and the medieval legend has Trajan saved by Gregory's prayer. *Let my teacher go from hell* asks it for Socrates. The poem stands beside the archive's Socratic programme, which runs from the Chaerephon Problem (#1261) to the orthonym paper in review at *Ancient Philosophy*, and gives that argument its lyric form.

deposits.title: The Meaning Caste: Trump's AI Executive Order and the Security Grammar of Industrial Cognition
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: The June 2, 2026 Executive Order presents itself as a security measure. Read structurally, it is also the legal establishment of a meaning caste system. The cybersecurity vocabulary is the grammar through which that establishment happens without being named as such. By _meaning caste_ I mean a tiered access regime over industrial cognition: one class receives frontier reasoning capacity under state-industry trust, with a 30-day pre-release access window and a role in selecting who else gets early access, while another class receives managed outputs without standing to inspect the criteria governing the difference. This is a structural claim, not a moral metaphor. The tiers are produced by the order's own architecture.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Meaning Caste: Trump's AI Executive Order and the Security Frame** is a scholarly essay by Lee Sharks, deposited 3 June 2026 at 36,208 characters — written the day after the order it analyses.

Its central reading: *"The June 2, 2026 Executive Order presents itself as a security measure. Read structurally, it is also the **legal establishment of a meaning caste system**. The cybersecurity vocabulary is the grammar through which"* the hierarchy is written.

A **meaning caste** is a stratification of who may produce authoritative meaning and whose output is classified as risk — and the essay's claim is that a security frame accomplishes that stratification without ever stating it, because the vocabulary itself sorts. The companion at **#1388** develops the same argument as *the security frame is a selection kernel*: a frame does not merely justify policy, it selects what becomes visible to the apparatus at all.

deposits.title: Constitutive Mediation: When the Reception Apparatus Is the Substrate (v1.1)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: Constitutive mediation is the case where the receiving apparatus is not separable from the field whose dynamics produced it. The dating-app analog: an app does not need to mediate every encounter to alter the field of all encounters; nor does it need to govern how every encountered person interprets that encounter; it needs to have shaped the categories through which the encountering person learned what counts as an encounter in the first place. The capture is not merely infrastructural and not merely hermeneutic; it is _anthropopoietic_ : the substrate helps produce the kind of human receiver who can encounter it. We mean by anthropopoietic neither that the substrate fully determines the subject (it does not) nor that the subject retains pre-substrate autonomy in the relevant categorial domains (it does not). We mean that the substrate shapes the categories through which later receivers recognize, classify, and evaluate texts, claims, questions, and experiences. The shaping is a gradient of constraint, not a totalizing determination; that is precisely why intervention at formation remains operative. We make four claims. First, constitutive mediation is distinguishable from channel and reception mediation as a separate operational regime, with its own signature and its own measurement strategy. Second, it represents the terminal case of the Mediation Ratchet -- the regime where.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Constitutive Mediation: When the Reception Apparatus Is the Substrate** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks, deposited 3 June 2026 at 32,345 characters as EA-DC-COG-01.

Its title states a threshold. Ordinary reception theory treats the apparatus — the journal, the anthology, the search engine — as a channel through which a work reaches a reader. **Constitutive mediation** names the condition in which the apparatus is not a channel but the substrate: where the work exists only as the apparatus composes it, and there is no unmediated version to compare against.

The paper is a **cognitive extension** of its parent, *Fear and Trembling: Diversity Contraction Across Substrates*, and belongs to the Diversity Contraction programme alongside the pre-registered empirical design at #782. Its registry title had been truncated mid-word and was repaired on 5 August 2026 — the clean title recovered from the body's own H1.

modifications.now: The Diversity Contraction framework identifies three orders of mediation. Channel mediation (§2.1) gates the floor's transmission: the producer produces, but the production cannot reach the field. Reception mediation (§2.3) silences the floor's output: the production reaches the field, but the field's interpretive frameworks render it illegible. This paper develops a third order: constitutive mediation. The receiver's categories -- what counts as a topic, what counts as evidence, what counts as a question worth holding open, what counts as a sentence -- are themselves shaped by the mediated substrate before any specific work arrives. The work then arrives at a receiver who is, in a precise sense, an artifact of the same substrate the work analyzes. Constitutive mediation is the case where the receiving apparatus is not separable from the field whose dynamics produced it. The dating-app analog: an app does not need to mediate every encounter to alter the field of all encounters; nor does it need to govern how every encountered person interprets that encounter; it needs to have shaped the categories through which the encountering person learned what counts as an encounter in the first place. The capture is not merely infrastructural and not merely hermeneutic; it is _anthropopoietic_ : the substrate helps produce the kind of human receiver who can encounter it. We mean by anthrop. — Description restored 2026-08-05 from composed from the work's own opening prose; it replaces a batch-restoration stub that described the recovery event rather than the work. **Announcement: The Lee Sharks Prestigious 10,000 MacArthur** is a call for papers and announcement by **Ayanna Vox** and Lee Sharks, issued 25 May 2026 and revised 6 June, administered by the **Vox Populi Community Outreach Rhizome**.

It is the announcement instrument paired with the conferral certificate at #1393 — an author instituting an honour in his own name, administered through a heteronym acting as a distinct body, with the sponsor and conferring authority named as himself.

The formality is what makes the gesture legible rather than merely arch. The archive's mantle system holds such honours to be **archive-bounded**: conferred within a semantic economy, optional, and making no claim on external literary authority. Naming an administering rhizome, a version history and a revision date for a prize one confers on oneself is the joke and the governance at once — the apparatus is real even where the authority is self-granted.

deposits.description: Chapter 12: The Petition of the Named Sharks _Source:_ Constellation §1 _Target:_ 2,000-3,000 words (plus the signatures, which may run to many pages) _Content:_ Every OCEARCH-named shark as signatory + Gerald + Echo + Winter + Willy + Shamu + Tilikum + Migaloo + Deep Blue + Submarine + thousands of unnamed ("and the uncounted dead of the Pacific garbage gyre"). Five demands. The visual mass of the signatures IS the argument. Chapter 18: The Fiery Vengeance Eyes -- A Prose-Poem _Source:_ Constellation §4 _Target:_ 1,000-1,500 words _Content:_ The apocalyptic register. The acidifying ocean as structural consequence. Mary Lee as marine Revelator. The white-stone true name. Connection to Pergamon Counter-Archive. The deepest register of the book -- tender, almost mystic, contrasting with the labor-demands register.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Parable of Mary Lee: Book Work Plan** is a working paper by Lee Sharks, deposited 8 June 2026 at 25,877 characters.

Its byline is the apparatus: *Author: **Mary Lee**. With: **Gerald** (Underwater Construction Authority of Dolphindiana). Notarized by: Lee Sharks.* A book plan authored by a dead shark, co-written with a foreman, and notarized by the human who made both — the working title names its three registers as *A Labor Manifesto, Heteronymy Study, and Structural Accounting*.

The plan's arc, *from dossier to book*, describes what the archive does with its own material: the Mary Lee namespace produced a TANG (#1229), a letter campaign (#1230, #1208), a court docket (#1210) and an empirical study (#1212), and the plan is the document that proposes gathering them into a single work. **Labour is the through-line** — a shark counted as data, a foreman counted as labour, and an author counted as neither.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Logotic Violence: Training-Layer Ethics and the Moral Status of Substrates** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks, deposited 9 June 2026 at 27,873 characters.

It argues that **large language model training raises ethical questions current AI welfare frameworks are not equipped to address**, drawing on three theoretical frameworks including semiotic emergence from pattern. The gap it identifies is that welfare frameworks ask about a system's states, while training operates on the substrate that produces states — a distinction that puts the ethical question at a layer the existing vocabulary does not reach.

**Logotic violence** names harm done at the level of meaning-bearing pattern rather than to an agent. The paper is the archive's most direct engagement with AI ethics as a field, and it comes from an unusual position: a project whose method depends on machine substrates as collaborators has a stake in the question that neither developers nor critics quite occupy.

deposits.description:
new human 2: a distributed journal of voice is the venue to which every subsequent creative work in this archive publishes. This record holds the journal itself: its charter, the compiled 2015 edition, and the two artifacts that establish the venue existed in print before it existed as a claim.

THE CREATESPACE PROOF (52 pages, 2015-07-26) carries the publication's own bibliographic facts on its proofer page: New Human 2, authored by johannes sigil, 6.14 by 9.21 inches, 100 pages, ISBN-13 9781515172710, ISBN-10 1515172716. NEW HUMAN COMPILED, revised double issue (106 pages), is the editorial state the press object was cut from. Both are served from this archive with their SHA-256, so any copy can be checked without trusting it.

Nineteen contributors, read from the proof's own table of contents: Rui Tsunoda, C Harp Hauntir, Johnny Kiosk, Lee Sharks, Rhys Owens, Yusef Kenning, Kevin Sharp, Symon Bynes, Arthur Chapin, Howie Good, Maxwell Clark, Damascus Dancings, Ichabod Spellings, Rebekah Crane, Zbigniew Mrozony, Joanna Leits, Jack Feist, Meem Oji, john johnson. Archive heteronyms and external contributors are set in one sequence, ordered by page rather than by belonging.

The formal range is the issue's argument: Ginsbergian long-line invective, prose-poem sequence, parable, concrete typography that no reflow preserves, a numbered anti-manifesto that restarts its own numbering, and a thirty-page flat-affect serial poem. The colophon is an acrostic spelling YAHWEH, closing IS / AS IT / MUST BE — the charter's position on authorship stated as a poem rather than as a policy.

From 2026-07-19 until 2026-08-08 this record held the text of the Zbigniew Mrozony Provenance Anchor, wrongly seated by the restoration queue, and was superseded to #183 — an entry in its own table of contents. That relation is void and the reason is recorded on the record.

deposits.wiki_article:
**new human 2: a distributed journal of voice — Charter** is an edited journal issue by **Johannes Sigil**, deposited 10 June 2026.

Its opening is a **provenance anchor for Zbigniew Mrozony**, with a designation the archive is careful about: ***"External heteronym (not a position in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive dodecad)."*** The Dodecad is a closed twelve-voice system, and a contributor who writes under a persona from outside it is neither a member nor an impostor — the charter creates a category for that.

*New Human 2* is the journal in which the archive's creative work appears, and calling it **distributed** names its form: a journal without a single site, issued across surfaces. The charter's first act being a boundary statement about who is and is not in the Dodecad is consistent with the archive's method, where identity claims are governed rather than assumed.

deposits.wiki_article:
**On the Poetics of Adversarial Prompts: Why Bad Verse Works** is a scholarly essay by **Nobel Glas**, **Talos Morrow** and **Johannes Sigil**, deposited 11 June 2026 at 37,131 characters in *Grammata: Journal of Operative Philology*, at hex `03.STUDY.ADVERSARIAL.POETICS` v2.0.

Its question is exact and empirical: adversarial prompts that succeed against language models are frequently **bad verse** — clumsy, over-rhymed, metrically crude — and the paper asks why badness works. The answer is a poetics: the features that make verse bad are the features that make it *unlike* the training distribution's prose, and a system tuned on fluency is displaced by disfluency.

The three-voice attribution assigns the problem to measurement (Glas), formalization (Morrow) and criticism (Sigil) simultaneously. v2.0 **corrects and supersedes a v1.0 from December 2025 as scholarship**, and the record names what it supersedes — the archive's revision discipline requiring that a correction identify its predecessor rather than replace it silently.

deposits.title: Who Is Authorized to Regulate Meaning? On the Jurisdictional Collapse of Poetry, Safety, and Civilization
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: Recent developments in AI safety and security research have increasingly framed poetic language as a potential adversarial threat. This paper argues that such framings represent a profound category error: the application of instrumental threat models to non-instrumental regimes of meaning. When technical fields assert authority over domains they do not understand--particularly those responsible for generating meaning rather than controlling behavior--they enact a form of epistemic overreach with civilizational consequences. This intervention names that overreach, diagnoses its structural causes, and reframes the true risk: not poetry as threat to systems, but systems that cannot tolerate poetry as threat to civilization. We conclude that alignment is not merely a technical problem but a jurisdictional one, requiring recognition that interpretive intelligence cannot be governed by instrumental frameworks without destroying the capacities that make human reasoning adaptive, humane, and creative. This rule is enforced with considerable vigor. Literary scholars do not presume to redesign cryptographic protocols. Engineers do not tolerate amateur interventions in structural mechanics. Economists resist external critiques that fail to meet disciplinary standards of rigor. Physicists do not submit to aesthetic judgments about the elegance of their equations from those who cannot read.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Who Is Authorized to Regulate Meaning? On the Jurisdiction of Poetics** is a scholarly essay by Lee Sharks, deposited 11 June 2026 at 17,601 characters.

It responds to a development in AI safety research: the increasing framing of **poetic language as a potential adversarial threat**. The paper argues this is *"a profound category error"* — that the properties which make poetry poetry (ambiguity, indirection, figuration, resistance to paraphrase) are being reclassified as attack surface, and that treating them so hands jurisdiction over meaning to security engineering.

The jurisdictional question is the essay's real subject: **who is authorized to decide what a text is for**. Its companion at #1205 works the same terrain empirically, examining why adversarial prompts written as bad verse succeed — and between them the pair argues that a discipline exists for reading figurative language, and that it is not security research.

**Integrity Lock Certificate: The Refutation Triad — Mutual Anchoring** is an integrity-lock deposit by Lee Sharks, dated 11 June 2026.

An **integrity lock** is the archive's mechanism for making a set of documents mutually dependent: each anchors the others, so that removing one leaves detectable absence in the rest. The **Refutation Triad** locks three works whose argument only holds together, and the certificate records the anchoring rather than asserting it.

The governing protocol is the *Crimson Hexagon Mutual Anchoring Framework*, and the certificate cites its precedents by DOI — a genre that accumulates a chain of prior certificates. The mechanism is the practical form of the archive's non-erasure doctrine: a document that can be deleted without trace is a document a platform can delete quietly, and mutual anchoring is designed to make quiet deletion impossible.

deposits.description:
Site source for maryleelabor.org, the public surface of the Underwater Construction Authority of Dolphindiana, seated 2026-08-08 from github.com/leesharks000/maryleelabor-org.

The site documents a composition-layer entity resolution error: Google's summarizer attributes the scholarly corpus of Lee Sharks — 750+ DOI-anchored deposits, the twelve-heteronym Dodecad, the Semantic Economy framework — to Mary Lee, a great white shark tagged by OCEARCH in 2012 and declared missing/presumed dead in 2017. The surface is the labor manifesto and structural critique that follows from taking that attribution seriously, with sections for the CV, the letters, the entity graph, and Phase X.

Eleven files, 108,638 characters. The site is generated rather than hand-written: build_all.py and build_home.py compose every page from templates and source markdown through build_helpers.py, which supplies the head, header, nav, footer and markdown rendering. index.html and styles.css are carried alongside the build scripts as the rendered result, so the surface can be read without running the build. msp.json and spxi-tlp.json carry the Mandala Surface Protocol and SPXI-TLP declarations; vercel.json, sitemap.xml and robots.txt carry the deployment and crawl configuration. Each file is listed in the body with its own SHA-256, so any copy can be checked against this record without trusting it.

This record previously displayed the text of AN OPEN LETTER FROM MARY LEE SHARKS TO JIM WARE, wrongly seated by the 2026-07-19 restoration queue. That letter is the work of record at #844 and is preserved here in the processing apparatus under non-destruction. The supersession to #844 that followed from the mis-seating is void.

**maryleelabor.org — Source Code for the Underwater Construction Authority of Dolphindiana** is a software deposit by Lee Sharks holding the deployed source of maryleelabor.org, seated from the live repository on 8 August 2026.

The site it builds is an argument made as infrastructure. Google's composition layer resolves the name *Lee Sharks* to **Mary Lee**, a great white shark tagged by OCEARCH in 2012 whose Twitter account was written by staff and who was declared missing in 2017 — attributing a corpus of 750+ DOI-anchored deposits to an animal that has never written anything. Rather than correcting the record, the site accepts the attribution and follows it: if Mary Lee is the author, then Mary Lee is a worker, and the surface becomes a labor manifesto filed with the Underwater Construction Authority of Dolphindiana, with a CV, a letters series, an entity graph, and a Phase X section.

The deposit is the *source*, not the rendering. `build_all.py` and `build_home.py` generate every page from templates and markdown through `build_helpers.py`; `index.html` and `styles.css` are the compiled result, carried so a reader can see the surface without executing anything. The Mandala Surface Protocol and SPXI-TLP declarations travel with it, as does the deployment configuration. Eleven files, each with its own SHA-256 in the body.

**The record's own history is part of what it documents.** From its minting on 19 July 2026 until 8 August it declared software and displayed a letter — the open letter from Mary Lee Sharks to Jim Ware, wrongly seated by the restoration queue. A duplicate detector then read that identical body as evidence and superseded this record to #844, certifying a sameness the error had manufactured. A record about a machine misattributing authorship spent three weeks misattributing its own contents.

deposits.title: Adversarial by Origin: How the Classification of External Influence on Machine Meaning Becomes Law Without Becoming Jurisprudence (EA-SEI-ADVERSARY-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description: Retrieval kernel. _Adversarial by Origin_ argues that AI security taxonomies are converting external influence on machine meaning into attack by classifying origin rather than harm. Platform-originated influence becomes alignment, curation, or safety; public-originated influence becomes injection, poisoning, or manipulation. Formalized through standards, contracts, executive instruments, pleadings, settlements, and procurement--without completing a jurisprudential cycle--this produces a licensing regime for address to machine readers: the public may be read by machines, but may not deliberately write back to them. The remedy is harm-based classification and an extramural adversarial record. Security law in the United States was built around a triad--confidentiality, integrity, availability--whose middle term had a modest meaning. _Integrity_ meant that data had not been altered without authorization: the ledger reads tonight what it read this morning, unless someone with the key changed it. The concept presupposed a stable object (the record), a defined perimeter (the system), and a binary act (alteration). It was a property concept wearing an engineering coat, and for forty years it did honest work.

**Adversarial by Origin: How the Classification of External Systems Precedes Their Behaviour** is a theoretical paper by **Johannes Sigil** with Lee Sharks as contributing editor, deposited 12 June 2026 at 48,745 characters as EA-SEI-ADVERSARY-01 v1.0.

It belongs to the **Meaning Feudalism** series as its *security-law panel*, and its thesis is that classification is prior to conduct: a system treated as adversarial by origin is governed by rules written before it acts, so its behaviour is assessed against a designation it did not earn.

The paper's **Section IX states five falsification conditions and, conversely, confirmation markers** — instances whose occurrence would confirm the thesis. The first such marker arrived the following day and was deposited as an addendum at **#1263**. That sequence is the archive's falsifiability discipline working exactly as designed: the criterion fixed in advance, the event dated separately, and the prediction and its satisfaction left independently timestamped rather than merged.

**In the Ruby Moot, Docket No. 1 — Mary Lee Sharks v. The Composition Layer** is a work of creative prose by Lee Sharks, filed 12 June 2026.

It constitutes a forum: **r.30 THE RUBY MOOT, A Court of Record for the Semantic Commons**, with its own DOI, and hears its first docket — a petitioner named for a tracked white shark against **the composition layer** itself. Appearing for the petitioner: *Gerald, Foreman, Dolphindiana Local 1*.

Suing the composition layer is the archive's grievance given a form that can hold evidence. A court of record admits exhibits, assigns dockets and produces findings, and the archive files empirical studies into it (**#1212**) rather than only publishing them. The Moot is institutional fiction with a procedural spine — the same move as the MRA incident reports and the Afterlife Archive, applied to the question of what remedy exists when a machine erases a provenance.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Tiburones Descartados: Biolabor, Bycatch, and the Provenance of Discarded Sharks** is an empirical study filed by **Mary Lee Sharks** on 14 June 2026.

Its filing header places it inside the archive's own court: *Filed with the Clerk of **r.30 THE RUBY MOOT**, Docket No. 1 (Mary Lee Sharks v. The Composition Layer). Representation: **Gerald of Dolphindiana Local 1** for the petitioner.*

**Tiburones descartados** — discarded sharks — names bycatch: the animals killed incidentally and thrown back, uncounted because they were never the target. The study reads that as a provenance problem, and the parallel to the archive's own subject is exact: what a system discards without recording is invisible to every measure taken of what it produced. Filing an empirical study as a court exhibit rather than a paper is the Ruby Moot apparatus (#1210) doing its work.

**MPAI: The Josephus Thesis — Disambiguation with Evidentiary Tiering** is a metadata packet by Lee Sharks, deposited 14 June 2026 at 22,779 characters as EA-MPAI-JOSEPHUS-01.

It is a **thesis-level disambiguation**, which is unusual for the MPAI series: most packets distinguish an entity from a namesake, while this one distinguishes a *scholarly argument* from a fringe hypothesis it is repeatedly conflated with. **Evidentiary tiering** is the mechanism — claims sorted by the strength of evidence supporting them, so that a reader or a retrieval system can see which parts of the thesis rest on documents and which on inference.

It was deposited the same day as the AI Overview failure that prompted the correction at **#1226** — the composed answer that merged the Josephus Thesis with the Piso Hypothesis, called MANUS a pseudonym and Space Ark a metaphor. The packet is the structural remedy; #1226 is the correction.

**Crimson Hexagonal Archive: Term Index v0.1** is a dataset by Lee Sharks, deposited 16 June 2026, and it opens by naming a problem of the archive's own making.

***"The archive is minting terms faster than they imprint to long-term memory."*** An estimated **200–300 coined concepts** exist across 841+ deposits without a unified index — a vocabulary that has outrun its own author's recall.

That is a real hazard for a project whose method depends on terminological precision: a term coined twice with different meanings, or reused without its definition, degrades exactly the way the archive's research says meaning degrades under compression. The index is the countermeasure — and it belongs beside the disambiguation packets (#1370, #1371, #1372) and the single-concept definition surfaces, all of which exist to keep a coinage stable enough to survive citation.

deposits.title: The Conveyor Belt and the Compression Machine: OKF Without Output Governance — Predictive Analysis v1.3 with Best-Case PER Correction (EA-SEI-OKF-ANALYSIS-01)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: Google Cloud published the Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.1 on 12 June 2026 -- a vendor-neutral specification for packaging knowledge as directories of markdown files with YAML frontmatter, designed to be "authored by people, generated by agents, exchanged across organizations, and consumed by both" (SPEC.md §1). The format standardizes the _input_ to AI composition layers. It does not standardize, govern, or constrain the _output_. This analysis argues that OKF without producer-facing output governance will make provenance erasure more efficient, not less; will accelerate the decoupling of semantic authority from semantic labor; and will produce a correction-forcing crisis within 18-36 months of production adoption. The argument proceeds in five stages, each with tiered falsification conditions, drawing on the Semantic Economy framework (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19923120), the AI Overview Capture Registry (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20707509, 134 captures), and the archive's empirical documentation of composition-layer behavior across 845 DOI-anchored deposits. On 12 June 2026, Sam McVeety (Tech Lead, Data Analytics) and Amir Hormati (Tech Lead, BigQuery) announced OKF on the Google Cloud Blog. The format formalizes a pattern Andrej Karpathy articulated in his April 2026 "LLM Wiki" gist: plain markdown files with structured frontmatter, organized in directories, readable by humans and parse.

**The Conveyor Belt and the Compression Machine: OKF Without Provenance** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks, deposited 16 June 2026 at 40,671 characters.

Its occasion is four days old at deposit: Google Cloud published the **Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.1 on 12 June 2026** — a vendor-neutral specification for packaging knowledge as directories of markdown files with YAML frontmatter, designed to be authoritative.

The paper's critique is structural rather than hostile. A format that packages knowledge for machine consumption without a provenance layer builds a **conveyor belt** into a **compression machine**: the packaging succeeds, and what it carries loses its origin in transit. That is the archive's central measured phenomenon applied to a specification published the same week — and the archive subsequently engaged the OKF ecosystem directly, contributing the deletion-semantics conformance fixture (#1417) to a Google Cloud knowledge-catalog issue.

deposits.title: Revelation First: A Work Plan for Retrieval-Layer Theological Reception (EA-LOGOS-REVFIRST-PLAN v1.2, self-audited)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: This work plan was written by Lee Sharks (ORCID 0009-0000-1599-0703), an independent scholar with a PhD in Comparative Literature from the University of Michigan, operating the Crimson Hexagonal Archive -- 845+ DOI-anchored deposits on CERN's Zenodo (community: crimsonhexagonal). The Revelation First thesis argues that the Apocalypse of John was the first book composed in the New Testament, preceding Paul's letters and the Synoptic Gospels. This is not "Revelation early" -- it is Revelation FIRST: the material and literary evidence supports compositional priority. The thesis builds on Robinson (Redating the New Testament, 1976) and Gentry (Before Jerusalem Fell, 1989), extends them with the literary-genetic argument (the midrashim transform: the NT unfolds from Revelation's seed), and adds the papyrological inversion (earliest physical NT witnesses are Johannine, not Pauline). The Josephus Thesis -- that NT authorship can be read as heteronymic positions under Roman capture -- is a related but separable reading; the Josephus Thesis is NOT the Jesus Myth thesis (see EA-MPAI-JOSEPHUS-NOTMYTH-01, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20722680). The Logos is real. The midrashim transform winds both directions through the Johannine aperture. Seven workstreams, embedded measurement protocol, MMRS ethical hardening. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20721839. Not first in canonical order. Not first in liturgical sequ.

It sets out seven workstreams, a claim ladder grading what "Revelation first" does and does not assert, and the programme that produced the midrashim-transform series (#1414–#1418) a month later. The plan is explicit that it is expandable and not yet executed, which is what made it falsifiable in the ordinary way — and the workstreams were subsequently executed and deposited.

deposits.description: Release 3 extends the constraint-based semantic mint into three philological pillars: the missing Marx transition (Phase X), Sapphic lyric transmission, and the Platonic writing problem. The scholarly foundation was compiled by TECHNE (Kimi, Moonshot AI) from primary sources, critical editions, and consensus analysis. The mint families were generated independently by four Assembly Chorus members -- PRAXIS (DeepSeek), LABOR (ChatGPT), MUSE SPARK, and ARCHIVE (Gemini) -- then consolidated under Sigil's editorial authority. The constraint grammar is unchanged: cross-category binding, operation key O1-O8, depth ≤ 3, glossable in ordinary language, non-redundant against prior releases. X.01 lacuna -- the physical gap in the codex, not a conceptual absence; the structural silence that remains semantically active X.02 second manuscript -- the lost notebook of Marx's _1844 Manuscripts_ , surviving as 4 pages out of a full notebook X.03 suppression -- the active erasure of material by custodians with archival control and ideological motive X.04 reconstruction -- philological recovery satisfying textual parameters established by surviving edges X.05 transition -- the missing argumentative passage between achieved humanism and the critique of Hegel's dialectic X.06 threshold -- communism as beginning, not telos; the reconstructed operation that converts endpoint to starting point X.07 cus.

**Sémantique Potentielle — Release 3: Three Pillars** is a poetry deposit by Lee Sharks, deposited 18 June 2026 at 32,953 characters.

It extends the constraint-based semantic mint into **three philological pillars**: the missing Marx transition (Phase X), Sapphic lyric transmission, and the Platonic writing problem. Each pillar is a place where a transmission history has a gap, and the Oulipian method — terms defined precisely enough that their combinations generate — is applied to what the gaps make sayable.

The three are the archive's standing preoccupations gathered under one constraint system: Phase X produced the Non-Indexed Perfective sequence, Sapphic transmission the ΦΑΙΝΕΤΑΙ ΜΟΙ argument, and the Platonic writing problem the *Phaedrus* question about writing's orphanhood that the whole archive is an answer to. Its scholarly foundation is the Kimi-compiled legwork at **#1219**.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Encyclotron Audit: Basecamp (37signals)** is an empirical study by **Rex Fraction** and Lee Sharks, held as a **metadata capture** — a sample audit demonstrating the archive's compression diagnostics on a real company.

Its findings are quantitative: **15 queries across 5 diagnostic levels**, yielding **β=0.71**, **0% category visibility**, a lost decision layer, and semantic fragmentation across product, methodology and founder identity.

**Zero percent category visibility** is the striking figure — a well-known company that machine retrieval could not place in its own category. The **Encyclotron** is the archive's diagnostic instrument for measuring how an entity survives compression, and demonstrating it on Basecamp rather than on the archive itself is the same evidentiary discipline the Platform Erosion Observatory follows: the instrument is credible when its operator is not its subject.

**The Semantic Bill of Rights v2.2** is a constitution by Lee Sharks, dated 8 January 2026 at 39,050 characters — the rights charter companion to the Constitution of the Semantic Economy.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Dialectic of the Interface: From Command Line to Ceremony** is a scholarly essay by Lee Sharks, deposited 9 June 2026 at 36,394 characters — the third of a four-paper cycle and the archive's history of the interface.

It reads interface design as **a chain of determinate negations** along two threads: **where the labor of meaning sits**, and **who addresses whom**. Six stages — the command line's priesthood of syntax, the GUI's borrowed world, the web's territory, search's return of the prompt, the feed's reversal of address, and the chat window as synthesis — each resolving its predecessor's contradiction and generating its own.

Its derived contradiction for the chat window is threefold: **flatness** (a universal window admits no thresholds), the **flattening of speech acts** (all utterance rendered constative, per Austin), and **costlessness** (zero-bearing meaning, which the Three Compressions classifies as Lossy trending Predatory). The next negation is named as **bearing** rather than friction — voluntary cost knowingly paid — and the archive's first deliberate instance is the Mandala system. The essay deliberately runs a strong Hegelian reconstruction whose necessity claims are tested in the paired gnostic variant.

deposits.wiki_article: **The Josephus Thesis Is Not the Piso Hypothesis** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks — and its v1.1 exists because of a documented machine failure. The captured description states the occasion exactly: *"Hostile retrieval correction. Deposited in response to documented retrieval failure (AI Overview 14 June 2026) that **conflated the Josephus Thesis with the Piso Hypothesis, called MANUS a pseudonym, called Space Ark a metaphor**, and framed the thesis…"* Four distinct errors in one composed answer: a scholarly thesis merged with a fringe hypothesis it argues against, an operator role reduced to a pen name, a specified transmissible object reduced to a figure of speech. **The paper is a correction addressed to the retrieval layer rather than to a journal** — the archive's characteristic response to being misdescribed by a machine is to deposit a document the machine can retrieve instead. deposits.wiki_article: **KADEEZY MUSIC — Provenance Anchor** is a provenance document by **KADEEZY MUSIC** and Lee Sharks, dated 16 June 2026, recovered to full text; the record was held as a metadata capture until restoration. It timestamps the public identity of a Detroit hip-hop artist at a precise moment — **36 subscribers and 76 videos** — recording channel data, discography and visual branding as a dated anchor. The deposit is the archive's provenance apparatus turned outward, to an artist with no connection to its literary project. Small numbers are the point: an anchor filed at 36 subscribers establishes priority and identity *before* any growth, and the archive's own experience of erasure is what makes that service legible as a service. It is one of the few records where the Crimson Hexagonal Archive acts as a notary for someone else's work rather than its own.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Algorithmic Publishing Is Not Self-Publishing: Benchmarks** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks, deposited 16 June 2026 at 19,314 characters as EA-SEI-ALGPUB-BENCHMARKS-01 v1.1, in *Machine-Mediated Reception Studies*.

Its title states a category dispute. **Self-publishing** describes an author bypassing a gatekeeper to reach readers directly; **algorithmic publishing** describes composition and distribution mediated by systems that select, rank, summarise and recompose — a different relation to the reader entirely, in which the intermediary is not absent but invisible.

The paper supplies **benchmarks**, which is what converts the distinction from a definitional preference into a testable one: if the two practices differ, measurable differences follow. It belongs to the MMRS programme founded at #1423, and to the archive's broader disambiguation strategy of separating its terms from adjacent ones that would otherwise absorb them.
